# s275 — Guide the orchestrator to sliver a slice in the relay

`slicer ai relay` gains a Slivers section and a Setup decision, and the role matrix gains a `sliver` condition, a sliver row and rules for eligibility, parallel slivers and escalation. The orchestrator may break a slice into slivers at its discretion, only when that is cheaper than one implementer, and confirms the sliver plan with the owner at Setup.

**Findings:** owner request, session 2026-10-14: slivers (parent:child) for relays · **Size:** M · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

The owner asked on 2026-10-14: an effort-1 slice of any size, and sometimes an effort-2 slice, can often be cut into effort-1, size-S slivers that Haiku implements well, with Sonnet taking over when a sliver fails. s273 and s274 make slivers tracked items; the orchestrator still needs the rules for when and how to use them, and the matrix needs to route them.

## Files

- `src/slicer/ai.py`, the relay text:
  - Setup: a bullet to decide whether to sliver. The default is no. Propose slivers only when the parent's effort and the cut allow it, and confirm the sliver list and which slivers run in parallel with the owner.
  - A new `## Slivers` section:
    - eligibility: effort 1 at any size; effort 2 only when every sliver comes out at effort 1; effort 3 never.
    - filing: on main before the worktree is cut, with `add --parent ID` (from s273) or one `slicer import` file; each sliver gets its own spec, size S, effort 1, with the parent's tree and pass.
    - order: slivers run in the parent's worktree; each goes implement, review, gate, handoff; then the parent gets one combined gate on the whole diff and its own handoff.
    - parallel: slivers with disjoint files and their own tests may run in parallel as the matrix rule allows, each with its own temp directory; slivers that share files run one after another; the orchestrator runs the full suite on the combined diff before the combined gate.
    - escalation: follow the matrix rule.
  - `--rest` and `INSTRUCTIONS` only if s271 left a relay pointer that needs the word.
- `src/slicer/roles.py`:
  - `RoleWhen.sliver: bool | None`, in `to_dict`/`from_dict` and `matches`, and in the "When" text ("sliver" / "not a sliver").
  - `recommend` infers `sliver` from `item.parent`, so the CLI needs no new flag.
  - `skeleton()` adds a sliver row first among implementers (haiku/xhigh, `when=RoleWhen(sliver=True)`, note "per sliver"), so first-match routes slivers to it without changing r1-r3.
  - New skeleton rules:
    - "Sliver a slice only at effort 1, or at effort 2 when every sliver is effort 1; never at effort 3."
    - "Slivers with disjoint files and their own tests may run in parallel, at most 3 at once; the rest run in order." The owner set the cap at 3 on 2026-10-14; projects change it with `relay-roles rule-edit`.
    - "A sliver that fails its gate twice, or whose diff falls short of the orchestrator's check, moves to the next model up (haiku to sonnet high)."
  - Reword the split rule: "a slice too big for one implementer is two slices or a slivered slice."
- `src/slicer/mergeroles.py`: carry the `sliver` field through the merge driver.
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: `relay-roles add/set --sliver yes|no|any`, matching `--split`; `recommend` output names the inferred sliver value.
- `docs/agents.md` (recommend JSON), `docs/commands.md`, CHANGELOG.
- `tests/test_relay_roles.py`, `tests/test_merge_roles.py`, and the relay-text tests.
